catalogue.title: How an order becomes a trade
catalogue.description: It prioritises immediacy over a chosen price; large sizes may sweep levels.

catalogue.title: Market order walking the book
catalogue.description: Larger orders can consume deeper and more expensive liquidity.

catalogue.title: VWAP from multiple fills
catalogue.description: It tells you what price you actually paid across several fills.

catalogue.title: Limit order resting and queue priority
catalogue.description: It controls the worst acceptable execution price but can leave you waiting.

catalogue.title: Partial fills
catalogue.description: An incomplete position may leave exposure or a hedge unfinished.

catalogue.title: Going long and short
catalogue.description: Its sign and size determine how price movements affect your account.

catalogue.title: Spread and liquidity
catalogue.description: Crossing the gap creates an immediate execution cost relative to the midpoint.

catalogue.title: Adverse selection
catalogue.description: A stale attractive quote can be selected by better-informed flow.

catalogue.title: Getting picked off
catalogue.description: A stale attractive quote can be selected by better-informed flow.

catalogue.title: Markouts
catalogue.description: It helps assess whether the price subsequently moved against the side that traded.

catalogue.title: Inventory risk
catalogue.description: An accumulation of units creates directional exposure and constrains new quotes.

catalogue.title: Inventory-aware quote skew
catalogue.description: Under the inventory rule, long inventory lowers the quote centre.

catalogue.title: Why one profitable run proves little
catalogue.description: It estimates an average outcome but varies between samples.

catalogue.title: Monte Carlo distributions
catalogue.description: It supports pricing, risk and comparisons when many possible outcomes matter.

catalogue.title: Standard deviation vs standard error
catalogue.description: It gives a scale for typical dispersion and for standardised scores.

catalogue.title: Confidence intervals
catalogue.description: It makes uncertainty around a mean visible.

catalogue.title: Winner’s curse / multiple testing
catalogue.description: Best-of-many backtests can disappoint on untouched data.

catalogue.title: Common random numbers
catalogue.description: It can reduce noise in the difference between their outcomes.

catalogue.title: What a call and put are
catalogue.description: It supports quotes, Greeks and risk revaluation.

catalogue.title: Black-Scholes inputs
catalogue.description: It provides one consistent relationship between price and sensitivities.

catalogue.title: Delta
catalogue.description: It sets the first-order stock hedge and contributes to portfolio risk.

catalogue.title: Gamma
catalogue.description: It explains why yesterday's delta hedge can become stale.

catalogue.title: Vega
catalogue.description: A stock hedge does not remove this exposure.

catalogue.title: Theta
catalogue.description: It separates time sensitivity from movements in spot or volatility.

catalogue.title: Implied volatility
catalogue.description: It allows prices to be compared using a model's volatility scale.

catalogue.title: Newton-Raphson + fallback
catalogue.description: The IV solver uses it to match an option model price to a quote.

catalogue.title: Delta hedging
catalogue.description: It supports quotes, Greeks and risk revaluation.

catalogue.title: Delta-neutral does not mean risk-free
catalogue.description: It can reduce small-move directional exposure.

catalogue.title: Realised vs implied volatility
catalogue.description: It changes option values and scenario risks.

catalogue.title: Covariance and correlation
catalogue.description: It retains the scale needed to combine risks across assets.

catalogue.title: Diversification
catalogue.description: More holdings help only if their risks do not all reinforce one another.

catalogue.title: Portfolio variance
catalogue.description: Position signs and co-movement determine whether risks reinforce or offset.

catalogue.title: VaR
catalogue.description: It summarises a model's loss distribution while allowing worse outcomes.

catalogue.title: Expected Shortfall
catalogue.description: It describes tail severity beyond the VaR threshold.

catalogue.title: VaR vs ES
catalogue.description: It summarises a model's loss distribution while allowing worse outcomes.

catalogue.title: Stress testing
catalogue.description: It asks about vulnerabilities that an ordinary risk model may miss.

catalogue.title: Greek approximation vs full repricing
catalogue.description: It asks about vulnerabilities that an ordinary risk model may miss.

catalogue.title: Correlation stress
catalogue.description: It affects diversification and is useful for diagnosing relationships.

catalogue.title: Model risk
catalogue.description: It connects numerical results to the conditions under which they can mislead.

catalogue.title: Regression
catalogue.description: It supplies a hedge-ratio estimate and residual for a stated training window.

catalogue.title: Residual spread
catalogue.description: It separates the fitted relationship from its current deviation.

catalogue.title: Z-score
catalogue.description: It expresses a deviation relative to its own recent scale.

catalogue.title: Correlation vs cointegration
catalogue.description: It affects diversification and is useful for diagnosing relationships.

catalogue.title: Spurious correlation
catalogue.description: It affects diversification and is useful for diagnosing relationships.

catalogue.title: Leg risk
catalogue.description: The temporary position can carry directional exposure the intended pair would reduce.

catalogue.title: Walk-forward testing
catalogue.description: It can create a backtest advantage that cannot be traded in sequence.

catalogue.title: Relationship breakdown
catalogue.description: It connects numerical results to the conditions under which they can mislead.

catalogue.title: Look-ahead bias
catalogue.description: It can create a backtest advantage that cannot be traded in sequence.

catalogue.title: Pair-mining / multiple testing
catalogue.description: Best-of-many backtests can disappoint on untouched data.

catalogue.title: Synthetic market: how prices emerge
catalogue.description: It marks holdings and provides context for the next decision.

catalogue.title: Historical replay: what is real and what is simulated
catalogue.description: It separates real data from simulated fills and prevents decisions using unseen bars.

catalogue.title: Scenario market
catalogue.description: It distinguishes synthetic model evidence from historical observation and controlled scenarios.

catalogue.title: Hidden scenario inference
catalogue.description: It distinguishes synthetic model evidence from historical observation and controlled scenarios.

catalogue.title: Why integer ticks
catalogue.description: Exact tick comparisons avoid floating-point ambiguity in price priority.

catalogue.title: Why deterministic seeds
catalogue.description: It lets another run reproduce a result or a bug.

catalogue.title: Why price-time priority
catalogue.description: Joining a queue does not guarantee that an incoming order reaches you.

catalogue.title: Why UI and engine are separated
catalogue.description: A presentation change must not invent a fill or alter a risk calculation.

catalogue.title: Why replay fingerprints matter
catalogue.description: It makes execution and accounting auditable.
